Se-functionalization of PAS promoted by hydrogen bond modulation In this work, with the purpose of constructing a novel polysaccharide functionalization system, PAS was firstly Se-functionalized in the reaction system with DES as the solvent, while related control experiments were carried out under different solvent conditions at the same time. Table 2 presented selenium contents and yields of SePASs obtained under different conditions. Due to the weak solubility of PAS in DMSO (Fig. 2a), the selenium content of SePASDMSO (970.98 µg/g) obtained by the selenylation reaction conducted in DMSO were significantly lower. When DESs as reaction media, the selenium contents of corresponding SePASDES₁ and SePASDES₂ were elevated to 1535.60 and 2126.70 μg/g, respectively. It indicated that adequate solubilization of polysaccharide had a significant impact on determining the efficiency of subsequent functionalization. DES exhibited the dual properties of hydrogen bond providing and accepting abilities, and this characteristic brought about the superior solubilizing capacity of DES, which was supported by the above experimental and computational analysis. Therefore, it was probable that DES could break the hydrogen bond interactions between polysaccharide chains and expose more hydroxyl groups. In addition, the high viscosity of ChCl-Urea impeded the contact of substrates in the reaction system under sufficient solubilization condition, resulting in a compromised selenylation efficiency of SePASDES₁. The excellent dissolving capacity and lower viscosity of ChCl-EG might cause the seleno-groups to be more easily introduced into the polysaccharide chains, thus enhancing the efficiency of the selenylation reaction. Consequently, DES with multiple hydrogen bonding sites was capable of being a new type of selenylation medium. On the basis of the promising Se-functionalization effect of DES system, the co-solvent effect on the selenylation efficiency of PAS in DES/DMSO binary mixed solvents system was further explored. The selenium contents of SePAS₁ and SePAS₂ were 1947.46 and 4004.29 µg/g, which increased to a certain extent compared with the corresponding SePASDES₁ (1535.60 µg/g) and SePASDES₂ (2126.70 µg/g) obtained in pure DES systems. Additionally, the binary mixed solvents system was shown in theoretical calculations and analysis to provide more hydrogen bonding sites in interaction with PAS (Section 3.3), allowing adequate exposure of PAS hydroxyl groups. The combination of the above two factors could lead to a better nucleophilic attack by hydroxyl groups, thus favoring the polysaccharide selenylation reaction. Similarly, Harifi-Mood et al. studied the reaction of 1-fluoro-2,4-dinitrobenzene with piperidine in DES/DMSO binary mixed solvents and found that the increase of DMSO was beneficial to elevate the reaction rate (Harifi-Mood & Sadrzadeh, 2018). This relationship was likely to be related to the fact that high polarity solvent was more conducive to the dissociation of anions and cations, which was beneficial to the destruction of hydrogen bonds within polysaccharide chains by chloridion and the subsequent major degradation of polysaccharide chains by acidic reaction envi- ronment. This also corresponded to the finding that both solubility and selenium content showed a correlation with polarity of DES. Likewise, the study of Liu et al. reported that the hydrogen bonds between chloride ions of DES and hydroxyl groups might weaken the strong hydrogen bond interactions in wood lignocellulose, thus breaking lignin- carbohydrate complexes linkages (Liu et al., 2017). Furthermore, the evolution of chain conformation in polysaccharide Se-functionalization mediated by DES/DMSO was investigated using MB and CR spectrophotometric method (Prentø, 2001). With increasing SePAS2 concentration, the gradual decrease at OD664nm of MB/SePAS2 absorption spectra and the progressive increase at OD554nm indicated that the positively charged MB interacted with the negatively charged SePAS2, which proved that seleno-groups were successfully introduced (Fig. 6c). Following this interactions, a long-range forces involving water and MB molecules appeared to bring the planar cationic molecules relatively close to each other and form metachromatic complexes, leading to selenium polysaccharide more inclined to rigid conformation (Michon et al., 2002). Meanwhile, it was observed that when SePAS2 concentration was 0.2 mg/mL, a large increase in NaOH destroyed the SePAS2/CR electrostatic interactions and disrupted the tendency for λmax of SePAS2/CR to be continuously red-shifting (Fig. 6d), which suggested that the rigid conformation of selenium polysaccharide (Tan et al., 2020). Similar results were reported by Liu et al. that the upward trend in λmax of polysaccharide/CR was influenced by the increasing NaOH concentration, confirming the extended conformation of polysaccharide (Liu et al., 2016). According to the above results, it was found that the M_W of SePAS was related to the polarity of DES, owing to the positive contribution of the high polarity DES to destruct the hydrogen bond networks of poly- saccharides, which further affected the degradation of polysaccharides by acid environment. Additionally, the DES/DMSO-mediated introduc- tion of seleno-group rendered the polysaccharide chains towards more rigid conformation. In summary, it might be possible to prospectively modulate the selenylation efficiency and polysaccharide M_W simulta- neously by constructing task-specific DESs with different HBAs/HBDs and solvent properties, which also provided new perspectives for the selection of solvent systems for polysaccharide derivatization reactions. ## 4. Conclusion The DES/DMSO binary solvents with more and stronger hydrogen bonding sites could coordinate the disruption and reconstruction of hydrogen bonds within polysaccharides, attaining superior solubilization ability than DES. The polysaccharide hydroxyl groups were fully exposed and activated in DES/DMSO-mediated novel Se-functionalization system owing to the disruption of the hydrogen bond networks, which facilitated selenylation efficiency and rendered acid-dependent M_w reduction. The obtained SePAS presented a tendency of rigid conformation due to the introduction of anion functional groups. In summary, this study supported further development of DESs with regulable solvent properties towards solubilization and functionalization high-value exploitation of heteropolysaccharide bioresources.
